fix(local): defuse closing keywords in the merge subject; log the amendment

PR 558 review findings.

F1 (blocker, local/bin/pr_merge.py:689) — gate 7 (check_dependencies) scans the
PR body and the branch commit messages, both frozen before the merge subject is
built, while the subject adds a third surface that reaches the default branch:
the untrusted PR title.  GitHub honors closing keywords in a merge commit
message, so a title reading "closes #900" closed an issue whose open sub-issues
and deferred status no gate had examined.  New neutralize_closing_keywords()
rewrites every CLOSES_RE match as prose ("closes #900" -> "closes issue 900")
before the title is truncated — truncation could otherwise forge a shorter,
different reference by cutting "#9001" down to "#900" — and the same defusing
applies to the merge body.  As a last resort, a subject that would still read as
a closing reference is dropped in favour of GitHub's own wording, the same
fallback an unmeasurable delta already took, so this can never refuse a merge.
The regression test drives the keyword spellings, the truncation case and the
body through the real helpers and asserts CLOSES_RE finds nothing left.

F2 (changes, local/protocols/issues-prs.md:174) — the normative amendment now
has its dated EVOLUTION.md entry (2026-09-14, issue #557 as trigger), citing the
owner decision, the merge-subject rule, its cosmetic-by-contract status and this
F1 repair.  issues-prs.md states the defusing rule beside the subject it governs.

Refreshed onto github/main (258 commits, no conflict).  All 637 tests of
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests pass.
